subject: Post-deploy tethered smoke + telemetry sanity — rollforward checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeCorp SRE <sre+redwood@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-deploy tethered smoke + telemetry sanity — rollforward checklist

Hi Anoop / Edge SRE team,

Thanks again for the greenlight this morning. Per our cutover playbook, we ran the initial tethered canary traffic for the private deployment in us-west2. I captured the immediate observations and next steps below — want to align on whether we roll forward the remaining traffic or hold for a focused rollback drill.

Quick summary:
- Tethered canary window: 09:00–09:30 PT; ~1200 requests; p50 token latency: 28ms; p95: 132ms
- Telemetry: trace sampling enabled; 3 traces show KV-cache warm misses on long-context requests
- Errors: 4 5xx spikes correlated with ephemeral network flaps on one rack (see logs)

Immediate asks for EdgeCorp:
1) Confirm if you want full traffic at 11:00 PT or prefer another tethered pass after we patch the rack NIC config.
2) Please share any additional SLO thresholds you want enforced before rollforward (token latency, error budget burn).

I've attached the tethered-smoke-runbook-v1.pdf and a CSV with the sample telemetry snippets. Irene and Marissa — tagging you for ops/rollback checklist and customer comms respectively.

If we do not hear back by 10:15 PT, plan is to run a second tethered pass after the NIC patch and then meet at 11:00 for a go/no-go.

—Jordan

Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: tethered-smoke-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 14 pages), canary-telemetry-sample.csv (10KB)
From: Anoop Reddy <anoop@edgecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCorp SRE <sre+redwood@edgecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-deploy tethered smoke + telemetry sanity — rollforward checklist

Jordan — thanks for the quick readout.

Appreciate the details. We want to avoid blasting production until we understand the rack NIC flaps. Action items from our side:
- We've scheduled a NIC micro-patch on rack-7 at 10:00 PT; will confirm healthcheck by 10:10
- SLOs: keep p95 token latency under 180ms and error rate under 0.5% for a 15-minute window before rollforward

Please proceed with your second tethered pass after the patch and share the runbook step you used for cache priming. If that looks good, we'll approve 50% traffic at 11:00, then scale to 100% after a second verification at 11:20.

—Anoop

EdgeCorp SRE
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeCorp SRE <sre+redwood@edgecorp.com>, Anoop Reddy <anoop@edgecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-deploy tethered smoke + telemetry sanity — rollforward checklist

On Tue, 19 Oct 2026 at 09:21, Anoop Reddy <anoop@edgecorp.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the quick readout.
>
> Appreciate the details. We want to avoid blasting production until we understand the rack NIC flaps. Action items from our side:
> - We've scheduled a NIC micro-patch on rack-7 at 10:00 PT; will confirm healthcheck by 10:10
> - SLOs: keep p95 token latency under 180ms and error rate under 0.5% for a 15-minute window before rollforward
>
> Please proceed with your second tethered pass after the patch and share the runbook step you used for cache priming. If that looks good, we'll approve 50% traffic at 11:00, then scale to 100% after a second verification at 11:20.

Thanks — running the second tethered pass now (10:08 PT). Notes from ops:
- Cache priming: we ran the KV-prefix warmup script in runbook section 3.2 (pattern: 8x short-context + 2x long-context per key) — attached snippet in runbook v1
- During the tethered pass we enforced flow control: max-batch-size=16, reqs/sec=70
- Post-patch expectation: if rack-7 healthchecks pass, we'll re-run the tethered pass against the same canary hosts to validate the NIC change before any scale-up

Proposed rollback trigger (if observed within 15m window):
- p95 latency > 250ms OR
- error rate > 1% OR
- any network interface flaps observed on more than one rack

I'll attach the operational checklist we used. Jordan — can you call out the exact CLI command you want EdgeCorp to run for a quick health probe?

—Irene

Irene Choi
SRE Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachments: tethered-smoke-runbook-v1.pdf (section 3.2 snippet)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeCorp SRE <sre+redwood@edgecorp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-deploy tethered smoke + telemetry sanity — rollforward checklist

Anoop / EdgeCorp team — thanks, and great coordination. Final state:
- Rack-7 NIC patch completed and healthchecks green at 10:09 PT (Edge confirmed)
- Second tethered pass (10:15–10:35) met SLOs: p95 token latency 145ms; error rate 0.22% over 20 minutes
- No multi-rack flaps observed; KV warm misses reduced by ~80% after priming

Requested next steps I will execute once you confirm:
1) Approve 50% traffic at 11:00 PT — we will enable route-split1 and monitor the telemetry dashboard for 20 minutes
2) If metrics stable, scale to 100% at 11:25 PT and post a short bulletin to your ops channel

Quick health probe command for EdgeCorp (one-liner):
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <probe-token>" https://private-edge.example.internal/healthz | jq .status

Marissa — please prepare the short customer-facing blurb noting the successful NIC patch, the measured stats, and expected next steps.

If anything changes from your side, call me on the bridge.

—Jordan

Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
